info: I1 over-strict lexical gate (fail closed): a comment line added inside the snapshot With block (input 6130676a...) refuses UNRESOLVED:A7_NECESSARY_LEXICAL_BINDING:conn, because lexical_bindings.py:20-24 keys each binding event by the SHA of its whole enclosing statement source segment (here the With). A leading comment that shifts every span ACCEPTs. So the lexical gate is partly a source-text digest of the binding statement; the statement shape gates themselves are AST-semantic as stated. No correction required.

I2 otherSnapshotReceivers (remote_git.py:285 self.snapshot inside GitHubRepository, def at :173; workspace_git.py:167 repo.snapshot) carry blocksGrantForThisReceiver=true but are not in obligations, and callerClosureAccepted=not obligations ignores them. Both are git snapshot APIs, not NodeChannels, so there is no current effect. The local-alias NodeChannels receivers the reviewer tried in node_transfer.py are refused by the retained use-site guard. Optional: count them or record the resolved non-NodeChannels receiver explicitly.

I3 the owner census case caller-dynamic-purpose expects A7_PURPOSE_PROVENANCE, which the baseline already has (NodeDelivery), so its oracle cannot fail. Reviewer delta recompute adds A7_PURPOSE_PROVENANCE at observation.py [17,16,17,70] (plus the generic use-site guard), so the claimed result holds.

I4 BoundDatabase (db.py:112-133) is an existing database-shaped type: transaction(tenant) only compares tenant and yields the outer conn, with no new role/control-epoch/tenant-gate statements, and recovery_epoch copied from the outer db. The body's Database.transaction attestation is specifically inv.db.Database. The existing A7_DATABASE_OWNER_CLOSURE / A7_FORWARD_ROOT_TYPE_UNPROVEN obligations already cover it; naming it helps the future owner port. No census path shown here reaches NodeChannels with a BoundDatabase, but the unresolved roots are not closed.
